newsitem.title: UK: BBC Worldwide reorganises for global coordination.
newsitem.headline: BBC Worldwide reorganises for global coordination.

text.p: BBC Worldwide Ltd., the commercial arm of the British Broadcasting Corp, on Friday announced a restructuring of key elements of its management.

The plan includes the creation of a BBC Rights Agency to be the sole exploiter of commercial rights to all BBC programmes, and the appointment of Dick Emery to the new post of chief operating officer.

Bob Phillis, BBC Worldwide chief executive and deputy director general, said the reorganisation was essentially an integration. BBC Worldwide Ltd was previously divided into three divisions: publishing, television and learning.
Phillis said the BBC Rights Agency was essentially a joint venture between BBC Worldwide and BBC production, designed to project "one face from the BBC to the outside world."
"The need to build on the BBC's unique position of cross-media brands, and to exploit them, means we need a more integrated structure than we've had over the past two or three years," Phillis said.

He said the changes were designed to create a strong central team to support BBC Worldwide's businesses, to enhance expertise in key markets and to coordinate activities across the BBC's commercial arm.
One of the most important objectives was to achieve coordination across the international market, Phillis said.
Phillis said now was the time to restructure given major joint venture deals being negotiated with Flextech and Discovery.
The restructuring follows a major reorganisation in the BBC at large, headed by Director-General John Birt, announced in November.
"It's an extension of the process which John Birt announced last summer," Phillis said.
